core_findings: Hammond remains a real standalone municipal policing surface. Official City of Hammond materials still publish a police-division site structure and a municipal fire-and-police civil-service surface, which is inconsistent with sheriff replacement or a fake municipal target.

The Tangipahoa Parish Sheriff's Office is not a replacement Hammond policing surface. TPSO's own official 2025 news release describes collaboration with the Hammond Police Department, confirming separate active parish and city agencies.
The repo crosswalk is structurally clean rather than suspicious. LA0530100 maps exclusively to 22:municipal:place:2232755 with no competing routed local-police row.

Repo continuity is real through 2022 and then breaks hard. The canonical Hammond agency row carries positive annual totals in every year 2018-2022, then collapses to zero-count rows with months_reported = 0 in 2023 and 2024.

The public publication trail also breaks after 2021. Hammond Police Department has an official city-hosted UCR / Crime Stats PDF through 2021, but this packet did not locate a later official 2022-2024 Hammond city offense table on the city site.

Louisiana's official 2023 crime report still lists Hammond P.D. in the Tangipahoa LIBRS participation roster, but the public PDF does not yield a recoverable Hammond city offense row in the published agency tables. That reads as public publication failure or omission, not as agency disappearance.

The current 2024 all-fill state is therefore best classified as a valid-target continuity/publication failure on LA0530100. It is not evidence of sheriff takeover, target invalidity, or a routing geometry mistake.
